packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - unverified image-only reading

EXPOSURE / RULES
No proposed identification or prior reading was present in my context. I opened only PROMPT.md and the ten image files of this packet. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

GENERAL NOTE
The packet holds ten images. The odd-numbered ones are reduced overviews (with grey scale and mm rule), each followed by an even-numbered native-resolution view of the same face. Each pair is described and transcribed separately below, in the order viewed.

==== image-001 (overview) / image-002 (native) ====
LAYOUT (observation)
A very small, irregular torn scrap, about 4 cm wide by 2.5 cm high by the mm rule, cream paper-like material with fibrous torn edges and a small round hole near the top. Text upright. Brown ink frame-ruling is visible: one horizontal line near the top (above it blank = upper margin) and two vertical lines, which define a narrow empty band (c. 6 mm) between a LEFT text area and a RIGHT text area - i.e. the head of a two-column page, with the inner ends of the left column's lines and the first letters of the right column's lines (tentative: the narrow band is the intercolumn; it could also be a ruled margin with a marginal note to the right).
Script: a small rounded cursive book hand in dark brown ink, with suspension strokes. One thin RED horizontal stroke lies under the second line of the right-hand area (underlining; tentatively marking a lemma or cited words). No initial, rubric or running title survives.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-002, lines counted from the top of the image)
Left area (line ends; left part of each line torn away):
image-002 line 1: [...]cam
image-002 line 2: [...]d(?) hoc re(?)[.]            (after "hoc" three letters "r/v", "e/c", "e"; possibly "rec" or "vt"; and further right, inside the ruled band and slightly lower, "[.]ua"/"[.]na" - end of this line continued past the tear, or a separate insertion)
image-002 line 3: [...] de ꝯsec̃cōe(?) dist.          (i.e. "de" + a word written with a con-sign, long s, a suspension stroke and ending "-cōe", then "dist." with a suspension over "di" and a point: the shape of a citation "de (con)sec(ra)c(i)o(n)e(?) dist(inctione)"; the middle word could also be read "de sepacōe"/"de scp̄cōe" - uncertain. A small superscript stroke stands over the first word.)
image-002 line 4: [...]ñ(?) az(?) an . i(?)[...]     (short groups: a suspended "n"/"u", a group like "az"/"qz" with a descending z, "an"/"au" followed by a point, a minim with superscript stroke; a small superscript "m"/"in" stands above this line near the middle; cut by the tear)
image-002 line 5: [...] (only the top of a long suspension stroke at the torn lower edge)

Right area (line beginnings; right part torn away):
image-002 line 1: c̄o(?) d(?)[...]         (a "c"/"e" under a curved suspension stroke, "o", then a round letter with rising stroke, "d"/"a")
image-002 line 1a: o(?)                  (a small "o"-shaped mark just below and between, perhaps a superscript belonging to line 2)
image-002 line 2: ē(?) du(?)[...]         (letter with suspension stroke, then "du"/"dn"/"au"; RED underline beneath this line)
image-002 line 3: sinu(?) b(?)[...]       (long s + minims: "sinu"/"finis"/"sum"; then a tall letter b/h/l, cut)

==== image-003 (overview) / image-004 (native) ====
LAYOUT (observation)
Another tiny scrap, roughly triangular, about 2.5 cm wide by 3.5 cm high by the mm rule, same cream fibrous material; whether it is the reverse of the scrap in image-001/002 or a different piece cannot be told from the images (the outline differs, so tentatively a different piece or a different face). Text upright; the left third is blank (left margin, with only offsets or ink specks), so the lines here are LINE BEGINNINGS, cut at the right by the tear. Seven short line starts, widely spaced, in the same small brown cursive; the ink of several words is partly flaked. One RED-filled capital C/E-shaped letter (a rubricated paragraph mark or red-touched initial) stands at the right edge of line 4. No ruling visible.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-004, lines counted from the top of the image)
image-004 line 1: [...] ac(?)[.]            (at the very top right edge: "ac"/"at" plus the foot of another letter; the rest of this line is torn away)
image-004 line 2: etiam(?) .                (reads "eti" + a partly flaked group "am"/"qm" with a long final descender, then a point; "etiam"/"et tamen" - uncertain)
image-004 line 3: pō(?) ap(?)loy(?)[...]    ("p" with suspension stroke + "o"/"e"; then a flaked group beginning with a/e and p or s, with a superscript hook, ending in clear "loz"/"loy"/"lor" - e.g. "ap(osto)lor(um)"-shaped, uncertain)
image-004 line 4: uid'(?)  [red C/E][...]   (minims + d with an abbreviation hook above: "uid(etur)"/"mid'"/"nud'"; then, after a space, a capital with red infill at the torn edge)
image-004 line 5: g'm(?)[...]               (a g- or q-like letter with crossed stroke and hook, then three minims: "g(ene)r(u)m", "q(ui)n", "tm̄" - undecided)
image-004 line 6: is(?) [space] ꝑ(?)x(?)    (at the far left, by the tear, two dark letters "is"/"us" - they may belong to the margin or be offset; then a p with crossed descender (per/pro sign) and a small x/r-like letter above right)
image-004 line 7: co(?)[...]                ("co"/"eo", cut by the tear below)

==== image-005 (overview) / image-006 (native) ====
LAYOUT (observation)
A third tiny scrap (or face), roughly a tall wedge, about 2.7 cm wide by 4 cm high by the mm rule, same material, torn on all sides, with a small hole in line 6. Text upright, seven lines, none complete at either end (both sides torn), so these are mid-line pieces of about 8-14 letters each. Script: the same kind of small rounded cursive book hand in dark brown ink, here better preserved and more legible than on the other scraps. Line 2 is written entirely in RED ink (a rubric: tentatively a heading or reference line, since it includes points and what looks like a numeral); a further red letter stands isolated at the far right edge at the same height. Line spacing is generous. No ruling, initial or marginal note visible.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-006, lines counted from the top of the image)
image-006 line 1: [...]supp'm(?)[...]            (long s or tall stroke, then "upp" with an abbreviation hook over the second p and minims "in"/"m"/"ri"; e.g. "supp(ri)m-" or "supp(er)i-"; upper parts torn)
image-006 line 2 (RED): [...]ubz(?) . ꝯsd(?) . iij(?) . [gap] C(?)[...]
        notes: red ink. First group ends in "-bz" (i.e. "-b(us)"), preceded by minims/"n"/"u" ("-nibz"/"-ubz"); a red point; then a short group of a 2- or con-shaped sign, long s and d with a stroke ("ꝯsd'"/"2 sd'"/"xsd'"), a point, then minims with a long final descender, most like the numeral "iij" (or "m9"), a point; after a gap a red capital "C"/"E"/"D" at the torn right edge.
image-006 line 3: [.]ndebat̄(?) in tem[...]         (first letter lost at the tear: "-ndebat" or "-idebat" with a horizontal stroke over "at" (= "-bat(ur)"?); then "in tem-", cut)
image-006 line 4: et q(uo)dā(?) mir(?)[...]        ("et", then "qdā" with suspension strokes over q and a ("q(uo)da(m)"/"q(ui)da(m)"/"q(uo)d a(m)-"), then minims + r/v: "mir-"/"mu-"/"uiu-", with a stroke above, cut)
image-006 line 5: [..]turo fue(?)[.] l(?)[...]     ("-turo" with a stroke over the o or running back over the word; long-s/f + "ue" ("fue-"/"sue"); a dot; then a tall stroke at the tear)
image-006 line 6: [..]ne ad specu(?)[...]          ("-ne"/"-me", "ad" (written with a round d), then a word with a large looped long s + "pecu"/"pecc"/"peca"; a hole and smudge below the s; cut at right)
image-006 line 7: [..]i(?) sem(?)[...]             (a letter with a horizontal stroke above it at the left ("ī"/"n̄"/"ū"), then long s + "em"/"en": "sem-"/"sen-"; cut by the tear below and right)

==== image-007 (overview) / image-008 (native) ====
LAYOUT (observation)
Two tiny, crumpled, stained scraps lying one above the other with a gap between them (together about 3 cm wide by 4 cm high by the mm rule); the lower one is rotated relative to the upper (its writing runs diagonally, falling to the right), so their relative position and whether they join is not established. Material cream, fibrous, with brown staining, delamination and a hole (black, with loose fibres) in the middle of the upper scrap. The writing is a small, quick, pale grey-brown cursive, more current than the hand in image-006, with long looping descenders - tentatively a different, more informal hand (gloss, note or documentary script) than the scraps in image-002/004/006, but with so few letters this is not secure. A thin vertical ruled or drawn line runs down the right part of the upper scrap; text stands on both sides of it. No red, no initial.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-008, lines counted from the top of the image)
Upper scrap:
image-008 line 1: [...]m(?) b(?)[...]                  (minims and a tall b/h/k at the torn top edge)
image-008 line 2: [.]om(?) p'(?)  [.]eb(?)z(?)[...]       ("-om"/"-oni" with a rising hook, then a p- or long-s-shaped letter with a curl; after a space a group with crossed strokes and tall letters, "ebz"/"sth"/"ffz")
image-008 line 3: Soi(?)/hoi(?) [hole] b(?)mi(?)[.]       (a group in a looped enclosing stroke at the left, "Soi"/"loy"/"hoy"; hole; then "bmi"/"bni"/"lmi" + trace, before the vertical line)
image-008 line 4: [..]m(?)[..] p(?)[..]s(?) oy(?)         (pale minims at left on a delaminated patch; a letter with a long descender; then "oy"/"oz"/"ou")
image-008 line 5: [...] z(?)l(?) . ē(?)/c̄(?) [...]        (a tall stroke with a z-like foot; a dot; a round letter with a stroke through or over it, at the vertical line)
Lower scrap (writing slanted):
image-008 line 6: [...]i(?)[...]                         (trace at the upper torn edge)
image-008 line 7: [...]o(?)e(?)o(?)[...]                 (three or four round letters, "aeo"/"oco"/"deo")
image-008 line 8: [..]u(?)o(?)[.] [...] u(?)[hole]       ("uo"/"no" at left, a v/u-like letter by the small hole)
  -- rest of the lower scrap blank or stained --
Nothing here is a secure reading; these are letter shapes only.

==== image-009 (overview) / image-010 (native) ====
LAYOUT (observation)
Two tiny scraps, one above the other, whose outlines and the hole in the upper one mirror those in image-008: this is evidently the OTHER FACE of the two scraps in image-007/008 (observation from matching outline and hole; the lower scrap is again rotated). The surface is whitish, fuzzy and largely delaminated; only the top of the upper scrap carries legible ink - three short line starts/pieces in a brown cursive with larger letters than the image-008 face. The lower scrap shows only faint grey-brown traces. No red, no ruling.

TRANSCRIPTION (image-010, lines counted from the top of the image)
Upper scrap:
image-010 line 1: [...] Bo(?)tz(?)/Sotq(?)[...]          (a capital B- or S-like letter with a bar from the left, then "o", a c/t-like letter and a final letter with a descender, q/z/g; cut at the top and right)
image-010 line 2: [.]r(?) J(?)ppa(?) d(?)[...]             (small "r"/"z" at the left; a tall J/T/I-shaped capital with a top bar; then "pp" with long descenders and "a"/"e"/"ic" - "ppa"/"ppe"/"ppic"; further right, after a gap, a tall letter d/l with a descender-like tail)
image-010 line 3: O(?)z(?)/dz(?) [...]                    (a round letter joined to a z/7-shaped stroke with a tail, at the left; the rest of the line is lost in the delaminated surface and the hole)
  -- remainder of upper scrap: grey smudges, no letters recoverable --
Lower scrap:
image-010 lines 4-6: [illegible - faint traces of two or three lines, including a possible "e"/"c" and minims near the small hole; no letter secure]

==== OVERALL: SELECTION, RELATIONS BETWEEN THE IMAGES, WHAT REMAINS UNREAD ====
- Every visible line on all five native images was attempted; none was deliberately left unread. No scrap carries ten lines; the largest runs are seven short line-pieces (image-004, image-006).
- The only passages legible enough to be worth checking against a source are:
  (a) image-006 lines 3-7: "[.]ndebat(ur?) in tem[...] / et q(uo)da(m)(?) mir(?)[...] / [..]turo fue(?)[...] / [..]ne ad specu(?)[...] / [..] sem(?)[...]", preceded by a RED line (image-006 line 2) containing "-bz ." and what looks like a numeral "iij";
  (b) image-002 left area line 3: "de" + an abbreviated word ending "-cōe" + "dist." (citation-shaped), with "[...]cam" and "hoc" in the lines above.
- Physical relations (tentative, from outlines only): image-009/010 is the reverse of image-007/008 (matching hole and mirrored outline - fairly secure). Image-005/006 may be the reverse of image-003/004 (the outlines look like mirror images, and the red letter at the right edge of image-004 line 4 would lie near the red rubric line of image-006) - not secure. Image-001/002 has no evident reverse in the packet. If so, the packet contains three physical items, one of them in two pieces.
- Scripts: image-002, -004 and -006 look like one kind of small rounded cursive book hand with red rubrication/underlining and frame ruling; image-008 and -010 are in a faster, paler cursive and may be a different hand or a later annotation. I draw no conclusion from this.

LIMITATIONS
- All pieces are torn scraps of a few square centimetres; every line is truncated at one or both ends, and no line can be joined to another scrap.
- Ink flaking (image-004), delamination and staining (image-008, -010), and a hole through the upper scrap of image-008/010.
- Orientation of the lower scrap in image-008/010 is uncertain (photographed rotated); I read it as it lies.
- Column structure is visible only in image-002 (two ruled verticals); elsewhere the crop shows only a margin on one side.
- Image resolution is good; the limits are the size and state of the fragments.
- Unverified image reading.
